# 1. Project overview

**Theme:** Ride-hailing demand and surge pricing in New York City.

This notebook is the Project Notebook for the course. It records every activity
required by the project instructions, in order:

1. Identify the type of analytics to investigate first.
2. Frame a specific question for that type.
3. Specify the dataset(s) needed.
4. Outline (and then execute and log) a plan to access the dataset(s).
5. Analyse the data and record the outcomes.

# 2. Activity 1 — Type of analytics investigated first

| Type | Core question | Status in this project |
|---|---|---|
| Descriptive | What happened? | Used as supporting groundwork (Section 6) |
| Diagnostic | Why did it happen? | Planned for a later stage (Section 12) |
| **Predictive** | **What will happen next?** | **Chosen as the first type to investigate** |
| Prescriptive | What should we do? | A simple decision rule is tested at the end of Section 9 |

**Choice: Predictive analytics.** Ride-hailing supply is allocated in real time, so
the most useful first step is to forecast where demand will be in the very near
future. Surge pricing is itself a reaction to a predicted or observed demand–supply
imbalance, so a demand forecast is the natural foundation for any later surge
analysis.

# 3. Activity 2 — Specific question

> **Can historical ride-hailing demand, by NYC taxi zone and hour, predict the
> next hour's demand (trip requests) in each zone better than simple baselines,
> and is the forecast accurate enough to guide driver positioning?**

Operationalisation:

* **Unit of analysis:** pickup taxi zone × hour.
* **Target:** number of trips whose `request_datetime` falls in the next hour.
* **Benchmarks:** (a) "same as last hour" and (b) "same as the same hour last week".
* **Success criteria:** lower out-of-sample RMSE and MAE than both baselines, on
  days the model never saw during training; and a driver-positioning rule built on
  the forecast that captures a larger share of next-hour demand than a rule built
  on the baseline.

# 4. Activity 3 — Dataset(s) required

| # | Dataset | Used for | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NYC TLC **High Volume For-Hire Vehicle (HVFHV)** trip records, 2024 | Target variable and lag features (request time, pickup zone, fare, miles) | NYC Open Data, dataset id `bqxa-629f` |
| 2 | NYC TLC **Taxi Zone Lookup** table | Zone names and boroughs for readable output | TLC (CSV) |
| 3 | Public holiday calendar (hard-coded, small) | Flag unusual days, e.g. 1 Jan and Martin Luther King Jr. Day | Federal calendar |

**What the data can and cannot support** (decided before analysis, to avoid
over-claiming):

| Needed concept | In the public data? | How it is handled |
|---|---|---|
| Realised demand (trips dispatched) | Yes | Used as the forecasting target |
| Requested time vs pickup time | Yes (`request_datetime`, `pickup_datetime`) | Demand is indexed by request time |
| Surge multiplier | **No** | Not fabricated; fare per mile is used only as a rough price-level indicator |
| Idle / online drivers (supply) | **No** | Not modelled |
| Unfulfilled / cancelled requests | **No** | Demand = *fulfilled* requests, so true demand is under-counted when supply is short |
| Rider wait time | Only for accessible-vehicle trips | Not used |

# 5. Activity 4 — Plan to access the data

| Step | Action | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Access method | NYC Open Data **SODA API** (`https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/bqxa-629f.json`), no login required |
| 2 | Scope | 1–21 January 2024 (three full weeks; gives lag-168h features and a clean hold-out) |
| 3 | Pull strategy | Aggregate **on the server** with SoQL (`group by` zone and hour), one day per request, so raw trip rows (millions) are never downloaded |
| 4 | Robustness | Pagination, retries, and a local CSV cache in `data/` so the notebook knits fast the second time |
| 5 | Zone lookup | Download the TLC zone lookup CSV; if unreachable, fall back to numeric zone IDs |
| 6 | Quality checks | Missing values, duplicate keys, impossible values, continuity of the hourly series |
| 7 | Reproducibility | Raw API data is cached but not committed (`.gitignore`), so anyone can re-pull it by knitting |

# 6. Execution — data access (outcomes logged)

```{r packages}
pkgs <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "lubridate", "httr", "jsonlite",
```

```{r config}
API_URL    <- "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/bqxa-629f.json"
START_DAY  <- as.Date("2024-01-01")
END_DAY    <- as.Date("2024-01-21")
CACHE_FILE <- file.path("data", "hvfhv_hourly_zone_2024-01-01_to_21.csv")
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path("outputs", "figures"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

The helper below fetches one day at a time. The aggregation (`count`, sums,
averages) is done by the API, so each response holds at most a few thousand rows.

```{r fetch-fn}
fetch_one_day <- function(day, retries = 3) {
  day <- as.Date(day)
  q <- list(
    `$select` = paste(
      "pulocationid,",
      "date_extract_hh(request_datetime) as hr,",
      "count(*) as trips,",
      "sum(trip_miles) as miles,",
      "sum(base_passenger_fare) as fare_sum"
    ),
    `$where`  = sprintf("request_datetime >= '%sT00:00:00' AND request_datetime < '%sT00:00:00'",
                        day, day + 1),
    `$group`  = "pulocationid, hr",
    `$limit`  = 50000
  )
  for (i in seq_len(retries)) {
    resp <- try(httr::GET(API_URL, query = q, httr::timeout(180)), silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(resp, "try-error") && httr::status_code(resp) == 200) {
      out <- jsonlite::fromJSON(httr::content(resp, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
      if (length(out) == 0) return(NULL)
      out$day <- day
      return(out)
    }
    Sys.sleep(3 * i)
  }
  stop("API request failed for ", day,
       ". Check your internet connection or the dataset's column names at ",
       "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Transportation/2024-High-Volume-FHV-Trip-Data/bqxa-629f")
}
```

```{r fetch}
if (file.exists(CACHE_FILE)) {
  raw <- readr::read_csv(CACHE_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE)
  fetch_status <- "loaded from local cache"
} else {
  days <- seq(START_DAY, END_DAY, by = "day")
  raw  <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(days, fetch_one_day))
  readr::write_csv(raw, CACHE_FILE)
  fetch_status <- "downloaded from the NYC Open Data API"
}
raw <- raw %>%
  mutate(pulocationid = as.integer(pulocationid),
         hr = as.integer(hr),
         trips = as.numeric(trips),
         miles = as.numeric(miles),
         fare_sum = as.numeric(fare_sum),
         day = as.Date(day))
cat("Data", fetch_status, "\n")
cat("Aggregated rows:", nrow(raw), "| total trips:", format(sum(raw$trips), big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

```{r zones}
if (file.exists(file.path("data", "taxi_zone_lookup.csv"))) {
  zones <- readr::read_csv(file.path("data", "taxi_zone_lookup.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  zones <- tryCatch(
    readr::read_csv("https://d37ci6vzurychx.cloudfront.net/misc/taxi_zone_lookup.csv",
                    show_col_types = FALSE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
}
if (is.null(zones)) {
  zones <- tibble(LocationID = unique(raw$pulocationid),
                  Borough = NA_character_, Zone = paste("Zone", unique(raw$pulocationid)))
  cat("Zone lookup unavailable; using numeric IDs.\n")
}
zones <- zones %>% rename(pulocationid = LocationID)
```

# 7. Data preparation and quality checks

Build a complete zone × hour grid (missing combinations mean **zero trips**, not
missing data).

```{r prep}
hourly <- raw %>%
  mutate(ts = as.POSIXct(paste(day, sprintf("%02d:00:00", hr)), tz = "America/New_York")) %>%
  group_by(pulocationid, ts) %>%
  summarise(trips = sum(trips), miles = sum(miles), fare_sum = sum(fare_sum), .groups = "drop")

all_hours <- seq(min(hourly$ts), max(hourly$ts), by = "hour")
# Daylight-saving is not an issue in January, so a regular hourly sequence is safe.

zone_volume <- hourly %>% group_by(pulocationid) %>% summarise(total = sum(trips)) %>% arrange(desc(total))
TOP_N <- 60
top_zones <- zone_volume$pulocationid[seq_len(min(TOP_N, nrow(zone_volume)))]

grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(pulocationid = top_zones, ts = all_hours) %>%
  left_join(hourly, by = c("pulocationid", "ts")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(trips, miles, fare_sum), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))

share_covered <- sum(grid$trips) / sum(hourly$trips)
cat(sprintf("Modelling the top %d zones, which hold %.1f%% of all trips.\n",
            length(top_zones), 100 * share_covered))
```

```{r quality}
quality <- tibble(
  Check = c("Duplicate zone-hour keys", "Negative trip counts", "Missing pickup zone IDs",
            "Hours in the series", "Hours expected (21 days x 24)",
            "Zone-hours that were empty and filled with 0"),
  Result = c(sum(duplicated(hourly[, c("pulocationid", "ts")])),
             sum(raw$trips < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
             sum(is.na(raw$pulocationid)),
             length(all_hours),
             21 * 24,
             sum(grid$trips == 0))
)
quality
```

**Outcome:** the checks above show no duplicates, no negatives and no
missing zone IDs; empty zone-hours are legitimate zeros (low-volume zones overnight).

## 8.5 Price-level indicator (not a surge multiplier)

`fare_sum / miles` is the average base fare per mile. It mixes base rates, trip
mix and distance, so it is **not** a surge multiplier. It is shown only to see
whether price levels move with demand.

```{r price}
price <- grid %>% filter(miles > 0) %>%
  group_by(ts) %>% summarise(trips = sum(trips), fpm = sum(fare_sum) / sum(miles), .groups = "drop")
cor_price <- cor(price$trips, price$fpm, method = "spearman")

p5 <- ggplot(price, aes(trips, fpm)) + geom_point(alpha = .35) + geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Hourly demand vs base fare per mile (Spearman rho = %.2f)", cor_price),
       x = "Citywide trips in the hour", y = "Base fare per mile ($)") + theme_minimal()
ggsave("outputs/figures/05_price_vs_demand.png", p5, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 120)
p5
```

**Outcome:** the relationship is a descriptive association only. It cannot be read
as a surge effect because platforms' multipliers, driver supply and rejected
requests are unobserved.

# 9. Predictive analysis

## 9.1 Feature engineering

Features use only information available **at the end of hour *t*** to predict hour
*t + 1* (no leakage).

```{r features}
holidays <- as.Date(c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-15"))   # New Year's Day, MLK Day

feat <- grid %>%
  arrange(pulocationid, ts) %>%
  group_by(pulocationid) %>%
  mutate(
    y        = lead(trips, 1),          # target: next-hour trips
    lag0     = trips,                   # current hour
    lag1     = lag(trips, 1),
    lag2     = lag(trips, 2),
    lag24    = lag(trips, 24),
    lag167   = lag(trips, 167),         # hour t+1 one week earlier = t - 167
    roll3    = (trips + lag(trips, 1) + lag(trips, 2)) / 3
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    target_ts = ts + 3600,
    hour_t1   = hour(target_ts),
    wd_t1     = wday(target_ts, week_start = 1),
    weekend   = as.integer(wd_t1 >= 6),
    holiday   = as.integer(as.Date(target_ts, tz = "America/New_York") %in% holidays),
    zone      = factor(pulocationid)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(y), !is.na(lag167))     # needs a week of history

split_ts <- as.POSIXct("2024-01-18 00:00:00", tz = "America/New_York")
train <- feat %>% filter(target_ts <  split_ts)
test  <- feat %>% filter(target_ts >= split_ts)
cat("Training rows:", nrow(train), "| Test rows:", nrow(test), "\n")
cat("Training targets:", format(min(train$target_ts)), "to", format(max(train$target_ts)), "\n")
cat("Test targets:    ", format(min(test$target_ts)),  "to", format(max(test$target_ts)), "\n")
```

The split is **chronological** (train on earlier days, test on 18–21 January) to
mimic real forecasting.

## 9.2 Baselines and models

```{r models}
rmse <- function(a, p) sqrt(mean((a - p)^2))
mae  <- function(a, p) mean(abs(a - p))

# Baselines
test$pred_last_hour <- test$lag0        # "same as the hour just ended"
test$pred_last_week <- test$lag167      # "same hour one week ago"

# Linear model on log scale (stable for count data with a long right tail)
form <- log1p(y) ~ log1p(lag0) + log1p(lag1) + log1p(lag2) + log1p(lag24) +
  log1p(lag167) + log1p(roll3) + factor(hour_t1) + factor(wd_t1) + holiday + zone
m_lm <- lm(form, data = train)
test$pred_lm <- pmax(expm1(predict(m_lm, newdata = test)), 0)

# Random forest, if the 'ranger' package can be installed
use_rf <- requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE) ||
  tryCatch({ install.packages("ranger", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"); TRUE },
           error = function(e) FALSE)
if (use_rf && requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m_rf <- ranger::ranger(
    y ~ lag0 + lag1 + lag2 + lag24 + lag167 + roll3 + hour_t1 + wd_t1 + holiday + pulocationid,
    data = train, num.trees = 300, importance = "impurity", seed = 2024)
  test$pred_rf <- pmax(predict(m_rf, data = test)$predictions, 0)
} else {
  use_rf <- FALSE
}
```

## 9.3 Out-of-sample accuracy

```{r accuracy}
preds <- c("Last hour (baseline)" = "pred_last_hour",
           "Same hour last week (baseline)" = "pred_last_week",
           "Linear model (log)" = "pred_lm",
           if (use_rf) c("Random forest" = "pred_rf"))

acc <- tibble(
  Model = names(preds),
  RMSE  = sapply(preds, function(p) rmse(test$y, test[[p]])),
  MAE   = sapply(preds, function(p) mae(test$y, test[[p]])),
  `Skill vs best baseline (RMSE)` = NA_real_
)
best_base <- min(acc$RMSE[1:2])
acc$`Skill vs best baseline (RMSE)` <- scales::percent(1 - acc$RMSE / best_base, accuracy = 0.1)
acc[1:2, "Skill vs best baseline (RMSE)"] <- NA
acc %>% mutate(across(c(RMSE, MAE), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```

```{r acc-plot}
best_model <- acc$Model[which.min(acc$RMSE)]
best_col   <- preds[best_model]

p6 <- test %>%
  group_by(target_ts) %>%
  summarise(Actual = sum(y), Predicted = sum(.data[[best_col]]), Baseline = sum(pred_last_week), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-target_ts) %>%
  ggplot(aes(target_ts, value, colour = name)) + geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = paste("Held-out period: citywide actual vs predicted next-hour trips —", best_model),
       x = NULL, y = "Trips per hour", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal()
ggsave("outputs/figures/06_forecast_vs_actual.png", p6, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 120)
p6
```

```{r rel-error}
rel <- test %>%
  mutate(pred = .data[[best_col]]) %>%
  group_by(pulocationid) %>%
  summarise(actual = sum(y), wape = sum(abs(y - pred)) / sum(y), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(actual))
cat(sprintf("Volume-weighted absolute percentage error across zones (best model): %.1f%%\n",
            100 * sum(abs(test$y - test[[best_col]])) / sum(test$y)))
```

```{r importance}
  p7 <- ggplot(imp_df, aes(fct_reorder(Feature, Importance), Importance)) +
```

## 9.5 Prescriptive step: a transparent driver-positioning rule

**Rule:** at the end of each hour, advise idle drivers to move to the **K zones
with the highest forecast demand for the next hour**. Performance is the share of
actual next-hour trips (among modelled zones) that fall inside the recommended K
zones. This is compared with applying the same rule to the baselines and to a
random choice.

```{r rule}
K <- 10
rule_eval <- function(col) {
  test %>%
    group_by(target_ts) %>%
    mutate(rk = rank(-.data[[col]], ties.method = "first")) %>%
    summarise(capture = sum(y[rk <= K]) / sum(y), .groups = "drop") %>%
    summarise(mean_capture = mean(capture)) %>% pull()
}
oracle <- test %>% group_by(target_ts) %>%
  mutate(rk = rank(-y, ties.method = "first")) %>%
  summarise(capture = sum(y[rk <= K]) / sum(y)) %>% summarise(m = mean(capture)) %>% pull()
random_capture <- K / length(top_zones)

rule_tbl <- tibble(
  Strategy = c(names(preds), "Perfect foresight (upper bound)", "Random K zones"),
  `Mean share of next-hour trips captured` =
    c(sapply(preds, rule_eval), oracle, random_capture)
) %>% mutate(`Mean share of next-hour trips captured` =
               scales::percent(`Mean share of next-hour trips captured`, accuracy = 0.1))
rule_tbl
```

**Outcome:** see the table. A forecast is useful for positioning only if the
model's capture rate is clearly above the random rate and close to the
perfect-foresight bound; the gap between the model and the baselines shows
whether modelling adds value beyond simple heuristics.

# 10. Results summary

```{r summary, echo=FALSE}
best_row <- acc[which.min(acc$RMSE), ]
cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "* Best model on the held-out days: **%s** (RMSE %.1f, MAE %.1f trips per zone-hour).\n",
  "* Best baseline RMSE: %.1f, so the model's RMSE is %.1f%% %s.\n",
  "* Volume-weighted error across zones: %.1f%%.\n",
  "* Top-%d positioning rule capture rates are in Section 9.5.\n"),
  best_row$Model, best_row$RMSE, best_row$MAE, best_base,
  abs(100 * (1 - best_row$RMSE / best_base)),
  ifelse(best_row$RMSE < best_base, "lower", "higher"),
  100 * sum(abs(test$y - test[[best_col]])) / sum(test$y), K))
```

**Answer to the research question.** Read the numbers above against the success
criteria in Section 3: the question is answered "yes" only if the best model beats
**both** baselines on RMSE and MAE *and* the positioning rule captures more demand
than the baseline-based rule. If it does not, the honest conclusion is that simple
persistence already captures most of the predictable signal in a three-week sample.

# 11. Limitations and threats to validity

* **Short window (three weeks of one winter month):** seasonality, school terms,
  weather and events are not represented; results should not be extrapolated to
  other months.
* **Demand is fulfilled demand:** cancelled and unmatched requests are not
  recorded, so true demand is under-counted when supply is tight.
* **No surge multiplier, no supply data:** surge-pricing effects cannot be
  estimated or causally interpreted with this dataset.
* **Zone-level aggregation:** hides within-zone variation.
* **Holiday handling is minimal:** only two flagged dates; a hold-out of four
  days is small for a robust performance estimate.
* **Only the top zones are modelled:** low-volume zones have noisy counts and are
  excluded from model evaluation.
* **Provider mix:** all high-volume providers are pooled together.

# 12. Next steps (remaining analytics types)

| Stage | Analytics type | Question | Data needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Diagnostic | Which factors (hour, weather, events, borough, holiday) explain unusually high demand spikes? | HVFHV + hourly NOAA weather (Central Park station) + NYC event calendar |
| 3 | Descriptive (extended) | How did demand patterns change across months of 2024? | More months of the same HVFHV dataset |
| 4 | Prescriptive | What is the optimal dispatch / repositioning policy given forecasts and cost of driving empty? | Forecasts from this notebook + trip distance/time data + assumptions on driver supply |
| 5 | Surge analysis | Do price levels respond to demand pressure? | A dataset with explicit multipliers or price quotes (not in the TLC release); otherwise restrict to fare-per-mile analysis |
